Envelope completes; the text field is never filled, never stamped, and the certificate/signed PDF omit it — with no indication anything was missed.
criticFindings.recommendation: Either (a) reject at validateForSend any field whose kind isn't end-to-end supported, or (b) extend the signer submit payload and stamping to collect+render text/checkbox/initials and enforce that all required fields are completed before allowing recipient_signed. File the chosen scope in the backlog explicitly.

criticFindings.title: No ESIGN/UETA electronic-records consent disclosure or consent capture
criticFindings.description: US ESIGN / UETA (and eIDAS for the EU) require that before signing electronically a signer is shown an electronic-record & signature disclosure and affirmatively consents, and that this consent is recorded. FineSign's getSession returns documents+fields and lets the signer apply a signature immediately; there is no disclosure step, no consent checkbox, and no audit event type for consent (AuditEventType in domain/src/types.ts:78 has no 'consent_given'). This is a foundational legal-validity feature DocuSign/Adobe Sign both implement and gate signing on. It is not listed in the PRD non-goals or the backlog.
criticFindings.scenario: A signer completes an agreement without ever being presented an electronic-signature disclosure or recording consent to transact electronically; a counterparty later challenges enforceability on ESIGN-consent grounds and the audit trail has nothing to point to.
criticFindings.recommendation: Add a consent gate to the signing session (disclosure text + explicit 'I agree to use electronic records and signatures'), record a hash-chained consent_given audit event with IP/timestamp, and surface it on the certificate. Make the disclosure configurable for self-hosters.

criticFindings.title: No automatic reminders, envelope expiration, or scheduler
criticFindings.description: The Envelope model has createdAt/sentAt/completedAt but no expiresAt and no reminder policy; AppConfig only carries a per-token tokenTtlMs. There is no scheduler/cron anywhere in the server to (a) re-notify a pending signer after N days, or (b) auto-void an envelope that has been outstanding too long. Automatic reminders and envelope expiration are standard, heavily-used DocuSign features and matter operationally (stalled envelopes never resolve) and for legal hygiene (offers that expire). Token TTL alone means links quietly die with no nudge and no sender visibility. Not captured in backlog or non-goals.
criticFindings.scenario: Sender routes a 3-signer sequential envelope; signer 2 ignores the email. The link eventually expires (TOKEN_EXPIRED), no reminder was ever sent, no expiration event fired, and the envelope sits in 'sent' forever with the sender unaware it is stuck.
criticFindings.recommendation: Add envelope expiration (expiresAt → auto-void with audit event) and a reminder cadence, driven by an injected scheduler port so self-hosters can back it with cron/a worker; emit audit events and sender notifications for both.

criticFindings.title: Completed-copy notification gives signers/CC no way to actually obtain the signed document
criticFindings.description: On completion the domain emits a 'completed_copy' notify to every recipient (envelope-service.ts:327) and the email says 'a signed copy is available' — but the notify carries no token, and the signer's original token no longer works: getSession throws ENVELOPE_NOT_SENT once status !== 'sent' (app.ts:249), and getSessionDocument/download are the only retrieval paths (the latter gated by the sender API key). So signers and CC recipients are told a copy exists but have no authenticated way to download it; only the sender (API key holder) can. DocuSign emails each party the final PDF or a working retrieval link. This breaks the 'deliver the completed copy to everyone' promise (ARCHITECTURE.md) and is a real delivery/UX-for-legal-validity gap.
criticFindings.scenario: A two-signer envelope completes. Both signers and a CC recipient receive 'Completed: … a signed copy is available', click their old link, and get a 409/expired error. None of them can obtain their legally-signed copy without contacting the sender.
criticFindings.recommendation: Either attach the completed PDF/certificate to the completion email or issue a post-completion download token (or keep the signer token valid read-only after completion) so every recipient can retrieve their signed copy.

criticFindings.title: No webhooks / event callbacks for integrators (DocuSign Connect parity)
criticFindings.description: Integrating systems can only learn envelope status by polling GET /api/envelopes. There is no outbound webhook/event-callback mechanism to push sent/viewed/signed/completed/declined/voided events to a subscriber URL. DocuSign Connect is central to how the platform is embedded in other products (the PRD explicitly targets 'Developers … integrate signing into their own product'). The deferred M5.4 item is about in-UI websockets, which is a different concern; server-to-server webhooks are not captured anywhere.
criticFindings.scenario: A self-hoster wants their CRM to mark a deal 'signed' the moment the envelope completes. Their only option is to poll the API on a timer, adding latency and load and missing the point-in-time event context.
criticFindings.recommendation: Add a webhook subscription model (per-envelope or global endpoint + shared secret/HMAC signing) that fires on each audit event, with delivery retries and a dead-letter path. The audit event stream is already the natural source.

criticFindings.title: Notification delivery has no retry/queue — a failed send after state advance strands the envelope
criticFindings.description: persistThenDeliver saves state, then fires notify effects with a single awaited mailer.send and no retry, queue, or dead-letter. If SMTP is momentarily down, the send throws, the request 500s, but the envelope has already durably advanced to 'sent'/next-recipient-notified with a token issued. The signer never receives the link, and nothing retries it — the envelope is silently stuck with no operator signal. There is also no bounce handling, so a mistyped/bouncing recipient email is invisible to the sender. For a platform whose entire flow hinges on email delivery this is a material operational-reliability gap.
criticFindings.scenario: Sender sends an envelope; the SMTP host rate-limits for 30s. mailer.send throws, the caller gets a 500, but the envelope is already 'sent' and the recipient 'notified' in the DB. No email went out and no retry occurs; the signer waits forever.
criticFindings.recommendation: Move notifications behind a durable outbox/queue with retries and a dead-letter, decoupled from the request lifecycle, and surface delivery/bounce failures back to the sender (bounce webhook or status).

criticFindings.title: No data-retention policy, purge, or GDPR/CCPA data-subject erasure/export
criticFindings.description: FineSign stores signed agreements plus PII (recipient names, emails, and — once fixed — IPs) indefinitely with no retention window, no purge/expiry of documents and blobs, and no data-subject export or erasure workflow. There is no API to delete an envelope or scrub a person's data, and no legal-hold concept. Any production platform handling agreements + PII in the EU/California needs configurable retention and a Right-to-Erasure path; the append-only hash-chained audit also needs a defined redaction/tombstone story so erasure doesn't silently break chain verification. Not in the backlog or non-goals.
criticFindings.scenario: A signer invokes GDPR Art. 17 erasure. The operator has no supported way to remove that person's name/email/IP and their document from FineSign, and ad-hoc deletion would break the audit hash chain and certificate hashes.
criticFindings.recommendation: Define a retention/purge policy (configurable TTL per envelope), an erasure/export workflow, and a legal-hold flag; specify how erasure interacts with the immutable audit chain (e.g. tombstoning PII while preserving chain integrity).

criticFindings.title: Documents and PII stored unencrypted at rest by the reference adapters
criticFindings.description: Uploaded originals, normalized PDFs, signed copies, and certificates are written to the BlobStore as plaintext (blobs.put), and the SQLite/Postgres repos store recipient PII in the clear. The self-host default (SQLite + local-FS blob store, NFR-1) therefore keeps highly sensitive legal documents and personal data unprotected on disk. DocuSign/Adobe Sign encrypt documents at rest as a baseline. There is no envelope-encryption or KMS seam in the BlobStore port. The prior security reviews covered transport/authz/token handling but never at-rest confidentiality.
criticFindings.scenario: An attacker who gains read access to the server's data directory (backup leak, stolen disk, misconfigured volume) can read every signed contract and all signer PII directly, with no key barrier.
criticFindings.recommendation: Add an at-rest encryption seam (envelope encryption via an injected key provider / KMS, or filesystem/DB-level encryption guidance) and document the self-host expectation; at minimum encrypt document blobs and treat the key as a required secret.

criticFindings.title: No backup / disaster-recovery story for the blob store or database (system of record)
criticFindings.description: FineSign is the system of record for legally binding agreements, yet there is no documented or built-in backup, replication, or point-in-time-recovery story for the local-FS blob store or SQLite/Postgres. The certificate of completion records only document hashes — if the signed blob bytes are lost, the hash cannot reconstruct the document, so a blob-store loss is an unrecoverable loss of the executed agreement. The audit hash chain likewise lives in the DB with no backup guidance. This is an operational + data-integrity gap for anyone running this in production.
criticFindings.scenario: The server's data volume is lost and there is no backup. The DB (audit chain) and blobs (signed PDFs) are gone; the certificates that survive elsewhere reference hashes of documents that no longer exist and cannot be regenerated.
criticFindings.recommendation: Provide backup/restore guidance and, ideally, adapter-level support (e.g. S3 versioning, DB snapshots), plus an integrity-check tool that re-verifies the audit chain and document hashes against restored blobs.

criticFindings.title: Shallow /health, no readiness/dependency checks, no metrics or tracing
criticFindings.description: /health returns a static {status:'ok'} without probing the DB, blob store, or mailer, so an orchestrator will route traffic to an instance whose database or storage is down. There is no readiness vs liveness split, no metrics endpoint (envelope throughput, signing latency, notify failures), and no tracing/structured operational alerting. For a production platform expected to meet an SLA and be on-called, this observability floor is missing and is not tracked in the backlog.
criticFindings.scenario: The Postgres connection dies but the process stays up. /health keeps returning ok, the load balancer keeps sending traffic, every request 500s, and there is no metric or alert distinguishing this from normal operation.
criticFindings.recommendation: Add a readiness check that pings repo/blob/mailer dependencies, split liveness/readiness, and expose Prometheus-style metrics plus structured error counters for the key flows (send, sign, notify, seal).

criticFindings.title: Uploaded (and redistributed) documents are not malware-scanned
criticFindings.description: Uploads are validated only by magic bytes + size (assertMagic). The resulting PDFs/DOCX are stored and then downloaded by other recipients and the sender, so a malicious PDF (embedded JS, exploit payload) uploaded by one party is redistributed by the platform to others. The backlog's X.7 sandbox item concerns only the LibreOffice conversion process, not anti-malware scanning of the stored, re-served files. DocuSign scans uploaded content; a production self-host story should at least offer a scanning seam.
criticFindings.scenario: A sender uploads a booby-trapped PDF; FineSign normalizes and serves it to the signer, who downloads and opens it in a vulnerable reader — the platform acted as the malware distribution channel.
criticFindings.recommendation: Add an optional anti-malware scanning port (e.g. ClamAV/ICAP) invoked on upload before a document is made available for signing or download, and document it for self-hosters.

capabilities.capability: Draft envelope creation & authoring (documents, recipients, fields)
capabilities.notes: EnvelopeService.createEnvelope sets status 'draft'; addDocument/addRecipient/addField each call requireDraft() (envelope-service.ts:90-97,134,165,186). HTTP routes POST /api/envelopes, /documents, /recipients, /fields (http.ts:132-194). App layer mirrors these (app.ts createDraft/addDocument/addRecipient/addField).
capabilities.recommendation: Solid foundation. Add ability to remove/reorder documents, recipients and fields (only additive today) and to edit envelope title/routing after creation.

capabilities.notes: EnvelopeService.send validates via validateForSend, transitions draft->sent, notifies the active routing group and mints per-recipient tokens (envelope-service.ts:226-246). Route POST /api/envelopes/:id/send (http.ts:196-199).
capabilities.recommendation: Add optional send-time settings DocuSign exposes (email subject/body, reminder/expiration config) rather than send being a bare trigger.

capabilities.notes: voidEnvelope transitions draft|sent->voided with a reason (envelope-service.ts:369-377); state machine allows draft/sent->voided (state-machine.ts:20-26). Route POST /api/envelopes/:id/void (http.ts:201-205).
capabilities.recommendation: On void, emit notify effects to active recipients (currently void produces no recipient notifications, unlike decline) so signers learn the request was withdrawn.

capabilities.capability: Recipient decline (with reason) voids the envelope
capabilities.notes: decline() marks recipient declined, transitions envelope sent->declined, and emits notify effects to sender + other recipients with the reason (envelope-service.ts:341-367). Route POST /sign/:token/decline (http.ts:225-229).
capabilities.recommendation: Consider whether one decline should always kill the whole envelope; DocuSign lets senders configure decline handling. Fine for v1.

capabilities.notes: routing.ts activeRecipients: for 'sequential' picks the lowest unfinished routingOrder group; recipientsToNotify + allActingSigned gate advancement; applySignature notifies the next group after each signer (envelope-service.ts:329-336, routing.ts:28-53).
capabilities.recommendation: None for core behavior. Expose routingOrder editing and a visual routing builder in the UI.

capabilities.notes: routing.ts: for 'parallel' every unsigned acting recipient is active from send (routing.ts:32). routingType chosen at create (http.ts:137).
capabilities.recommendation: Support mixed/hybrid routing (parallel groups within a sequential order) which DocuSign offers via shared routingOrder — partially possible today since same routingOrder acts in parallel; document it.

capabilities.notes: RecipientRole 'signer' (types.ts:17); isActingRole true for signer; validateForSend requires every signer to have >=1 field (validation.ts:50-53).
capabilities.recommendation: None.

capabilities.notes: 'approver' exists and is an acting role that gates completion (routing.ts:14-16), but there is no distinct approve action: approvers go through applySignature exactly like signers (envelope-service.ts:297) and are only exempt from the must-have-a-field rule (validation.ts:50). A true DocuSign approver approves an envelope without placing a signature field.
capabilities.recommendation: Add an 'approve' action/effect that advances routing without emitting a StampEffect, so approvers record approval in the audit log without a drawn signature.

capabilities.notes: 'cc' role never acts (isActingRole false) and receives the completed copy: on completion a notify effect with reason 'completed_copy' is emitted for every recipient including cc (envelope-service.ts:326-328). Fields cannot be assigned to cc (addField isActingRole check, validation.ts:40).
capabilities.recommendation: None functionally. Ensure cc recipients do not receive per-turn signing links (they should only get the final copy).

capabilities.notes: Each signing token carries tokenExpiresAt and applySignature rejects expired tokens with TOKEN_EXPIRED (envelope-service.ts:301-303; app.ts:127 sets expiresAt from config.tokenTtlMs). But this is a link TTL, not a sender-configurable envelope expiration date.
capabilities.recommendation: Add envelope-level expiration (expireAt on Envelope) with an auto-void/expired terminal status and reminder-before-expiry; today an untouched sent envelope lives forever.

capabilities.notes: No reminder scheduling anywhere: grep for 'reminder' in domain/server src returns nothing. Notify effects fire only on send and on routing advancement (envelope-service.ts:240,331); there is no scheduled re-notify.
capabilities.recommendation: Add a reminder policy (first-after N days, repeat every M days, stop at expiry) driven by a scheduler that re-issues notify effects to still-pending active recipients.

capabilities.notes: No resend endpoint or service method (app.ts method list has no resend; http.ts has no such route). notify() is private and only invoked internally on send/advance (envelope-service.ts:249). A signer who lost their email cannot be re-sent the link.
capabilities.recommendation: Add a resend action that re-issues (or re-mints) the token for an active recipient and emits a notify effect, recording an audit event.

capabilities.capability: Correcting a sent envelope (edit recipients/fields/docs after send)
capabilities.notes: All authoring methods call requireDraft() and throw ENVELOPE_NOT_DRAFT once sent (envelope-service.ts:90-97,135,166,187). The only post-send options are sign, decline, or void. DocuSign 'Correct' lets senders fix email typos, add fields, or reassign mid-flight.
capabilities.recommendation: Add a correct flow that reopens a sent envelope (or edits pre-completion recipients/fields for not-yet-acted parties) while preserving the audit chain; at minimum allow fixing a bad recipient email without full void+recreate.

capabilities.notes: No reassign/delegate method or effect; RecipientRole has no delegate concept and RECIPIENT_TRANSITIONS has no reassigned state (state-machine.ts:28-34). A recipient cannot forward their signing task to a colleague.
capabilities.recommendation: Add a reassign action that replaces a pending/notified recipient's identity (name/email), re-mints the token, moves their fields, and audits the delegation.

capabilities.notes: No template model or endpoints; grep for 'template' in domain/server src returns nothing. Every envelope is authored field-by-field from scratch.
capabilities.recommendation: Add a Template aggregate (documents + recipient roles + field layout) and an instantiate-from-template flow; this is table stakes for repeat business use and drives most DocuSign volume.

capabilities.capability: Bulk send (one template to many recipients)
capabilities.notes: No bulk-send capability; no batch endpoint in http.ts and no template to batch over. Envelopes are created one at a time via POST /api/envelopes.
capabilities.recommendation: After templates land, add bulk send that takes a recipient list (CSV) and fans out one envelope per row, with a batch status view.

capabilities.notes: No in-person signer concept; signing is exclusively via emailed per-recipient tokens (/sign/:token routes, http.ts:215-239). No host-plus-signer model.
capabilities.recommendation: Lower priority for an open-source/API-first product; add later as a host session that issues an in-person token bound to a physical signing session.

capabilities.capability: Tamper-evident audit trail / certificate of completion
capabilities.notes: Hash-chained AuditEvent log on every envelope (types.ts:78-104); events recorded for create/send/notify/view/sign/decline/complete/void throughout envelope-service.ts; certificate download route GET /api/envelopes/:id/certificate (http.ts:251-255).
capabilities.recommendation: Strong differentiator. Ensure the certificate renders the full recipient event timeline (viewed/signed timestamps, IP) to match DocuSign's Certificate of Completion.

parity.area: Field types & signing experience (DocuSign/Adobe Sign parity)

capabilities.notes: FieldKind includes 'signature' (domain/src/types.ts:25). Stamped end-to-end via STAMPABLE_SIGNATURE set in server/src/stamping.ts:24,106; both drawn-image and typed paths funnel through finesign-core signWithImage/signWithTypedNames. Auto-detected from AcroForm /Sig widgets and name heuristics (core/src/detect/acroform-fields.ts).
capabilities.recommendation: None needed — this is the strongest, most complete field type.

capabilities.notes: 'initials' in FieldKind (types.ts:25) and in STAMPABLE_SIGNATURE (stamping.ts:24). Placeable in the UI (FIELD_KINDS in web/src/config.js:24-28, DEFAULT_SIZE in Create.jsx:11). Stamped like a signature.
capabilities.recommendation: Consider letting the signer adopt a distinct initials mark rather than reusing the same signature blob; today one captured signature is applied to both signature and initials fields.

capabilities.notes: 'date_signed' in FieldKind; anchorFromField maps it to kind 'date' with dateFormat 'full' (stamping.ts:26-43). Auto-stamped with current date on signing (image path and a transparent-PNG date-only pass for typed, stamping.ts:112-138). Detected via isSignerDateField heuristic.
capabilities.recommendation: Solid. DocuSign also offers user-editable date and calendar-picker date fields; consider a manual date variant distinct from the auto-date.

capabilities.notes: 'text' is modeled with a value field (types.ts:74-76) but NOT collected or stamped. stamping.ts:102-104 explicitly filters text into 'skipped'; app.ts:455 warns 'some field kinds are not yet stampable and were skipped'. The signer UI (Sign.jsx) only renders read-only field-box overlays and a single SignaturePad — there is no text input at signing time. types.ts:24 comment: 'stamped in a later milestone.'
capabilities.recommendation: Highest-priority gap. Implement per-field text entry in Sign.jsx, persist Field.value, and stamp text via core. Without editable text, real agreements (name/address/title fills) cannot be completed.

capabilities.notes: 'checkbox' is in FieldKind (types.ts:25) but skipped in stamping (stamping.ts:102-104) and has no UI: it is not in FIELD_KINDS (config.js:24-28) so it can't even be placed, and Sign.jsx has no toggle control. Modeled only.
capabilities.recommendation: Add checkbox to placement UI and signer UI, store checked state (value), and stamp a check glyph. Required for consent/acknowledgement boxes common in agreements.

capabilities.notes: No 'radio' in FieldKind (types.ts:25). AcroForm detection recognizes /Btn type (acroform-fields.ts:40,80) but only classifies signature/date; radio widgets are never surfaced as fields. No grouping model exists.
capabilities.recommendation: Add a radio group field kind with a shared group id and mutually-exclusive selection. Needed for multiple-choice selections DocuSign supports.

capabilities.notes: No 'dropdown' in FieldKind. /Ch (choice) AcroForm type is detected as a fieldType (acroform-fields.ts:40,81) but never mapped to a usable field. No option-list model on Field.
capabilities.recommendation: Add a dropdown field kind with an options list and selected value; stamp the chosen text.

capabilities.notes: Field.required exists (types.ts:73), defaults true in addField (envelope-service.ts:213), and can be passed via API (app.ts:211). BUT it is never enforced at signing: applySignature (envelope-service.ts:286-338) marks the recipient signed with no check that required fields have values; validateForSend only checks structure, not completion (validation.ts). The signer UI applies one signature to all signature/initials fields at once ('Sign all fields', Sign.jsx:121) and cannot leave any unfilled or fill optional ones selectively.
capabilities.recommendation: Enforce required-field completion server-side in applySignature and client-side before enabling submit. Without enforcement, 'required' is cosmetic.

capabilities.notes: SignaturePad draw mode captures canvas strokes to a PNG data URL (SignaturePad.jsx:35-55, toDataURL). Sent as {kind:'image', dataUrl} and stamped via signWithImage.
capabilities.recommendation: None needed. Optionally add stroke smoothing / higher-DPI canvas for crisper marks.

capabilities.notes: Type mode offers 4 script fonts (config.js SIGNATURE_FONTS; SignaturePad.jsx:103-114) → {kind:'typed', name, font}, stamped via signWithTypedNames with width/height-bounded scaling (stamping.ts:59-83).
capabilities.recommendation: Good parity. Consider adding a live preview matching the stamped rendering exactly.

capabilities.notes: SignaturePad exposes only Draw and Type tabs (SignaturePad.jsx:78-81). No file-upload path for a signature image, though the API's image path could technically accept one.
capabilities.recommendation: Add an upload tab that reads an image to a data URL and reuses the existing {kind:'image'} path — low effort, moderate value.

capabilities.notes: No persisted signature profile. Signature is captured fresh per session in component state (SignaturePad.jsx) and never stored on the recipient/user. DocuSign's 'adopt your signature' + reuse across envelopes is absent.
capabilities.recommendation: Persist an adopted signature per authenticated user (or per recipient email) so repeat signers don't redraw each time.

capabilities.notes: Core has deterministic AcroForm auto-detection: detectAnchorsFromAcroForm + detectFields turn /Sig widgets and name-matched text/date fields into ready-to-stamp anchors (acroform-fields.ts:108-193), with signer-vs-non-signer heuristics (field-heuristics.ts). However it is NOT wired into the sender UI — Create.jsx only supports manual click placement (placeField, Create.jsx:81-92) and never calls detection. Flat scans with no AcroForm yield nothing (documented in acroform-fields.ts:16-17).
capabilities.recommendation: Expose a server endpoint that runs detectAnchorsFromAcroForm and pre-populates fields in the Create flow for review. The engine already exists; only the wiring/UX is missing. Add OCR/vision for flat PDFs to match DocuSign auto-tagging.

capabilities.notes: Name-based heuristics match sign/date tokens on AcroForm field NAMES (field-heuristics.ts SIGN_TOKEN, isSignerSignatureField/DateField). But there is no DocuSign-style text-anchor tagging (e.g. placing a tab relative to literal '\\s1\\' or 'Signature:' text in the page content) — only named form fields are matched.
capabilities.recommendation: Add page-text anchor scanning so senders can place fields by document keywords, not just pre-existing AcroForm fields.

capabilities.notes: No conditional logic anywhere. Field has no show-if/rules model (types.ts:63-76); no references to conditional/dependency in domain or server. Every placed field is always shown and independent.
capabilities.recommendation: Add optional field-visibility rules keyed off another field's value once checkbox/radio/dropdown inputs exist. Not blocking for MVP but expected in mature products.

capabilities.capability: Field format validation (masks: SSN, email, number, regex)
capabilities.notes: The only validation is geometric: drawnBoxError checks the box is on-page with positive area (envelope-service.ts:196-202) and page bounds in validation.ts. Field has no type/mask/regex/min-max attributes (types.ts:63-76). No format enforcement on any input.
capabilities.recommendation: Add validation metadata to text fields (regex/mask/required-length) and enforce both client- and server-side. Important for SSN/date/ZIP fields in the VA use case.

capabilities.notes: SignaturePad wires touch events (onTouchStart/Move/End, touches[0] handling; SignaturePad.jsx:30-33,94-96), so drawing works on touch devices. But PdfView renders at a fixed TARGET_WIDTH=680 (PdfView.jsx:4) with pixel width/height styles and no responsive/zoom handling, so the document view is not optimized for small screens.
capabilities.recommendation: Make PdfView responsive (fluid width, pinch-zoom, fit-to-width) and verify tap targets for field overlays on mobile. Signature capture itself is fine.

capabilities.notes: Placement is single-click-to-drop at fixed default sizes, not drag-to-draw: PdfView.handleClick emits a fractional point (PdfView.jsx:82-88) and Create.placeField applies DEFAULT_SIZE by kind (Create.jsx:11,81-92). No rubber-band sizing during placement.
capabilities.recommendation: Add drag-to-draw so senders can size fields, matching DocuSign's tab placement UX.

capabilities.capability: Edit / move / resize / delete placed fields
capabilities.notes: Placed fields render as static overlay boxes (fieldsOverlay in Create.jsx:109-127) with no drag handles, resize, reposition, or delete affordance and no click handler on existing boxes. There is no removeField/updateField call used in the UI (addField only, Create.jsx:81-92). A misplaced field can't be corrected except by discarding.
capabilities.recommendation: Add select/move/resize/delete for placed fields (and an updateField/deleteField API). Critical for a usable authoring experience.

capabilities.notes: Fields are assigned to a specific recipient (Field.recipientId, enforced to signer/approver in addField, envelope-service.ts:190-192) and color-coded per recipient in the UI (recipientColor, Create.jsx:103-107,121). Signer only sees their own fields (app.ts:257-271).
capabilities.recommendation: Good. Extend with the same treatment once more field kinds are interactive.

capabilities.notes: Per-recipient signing links use a random token; only its SHA-256 (tokenHash) is stored (domain/src/types.ts:52 Recipient.tokenHash, tokenExpiresAt). app.ts issueToken() generates ids.token()+hashToken(), resolveToken() looks up findByRecipientTokenHash and enforces tokenExpiresAt (app.ts:122-129, 237-245). Delivered only via email (app.ts notify(), http.ts /sign/:token routes, rate-limited). This is 'email possession' authentication — DocuSign's baseline. Note: the token is not invalidated after first use/signing (reused across notified/viewed/signed), so it functions as a bearer credential for the link's lifetime.
capabilities.recommendation: Keep as the default factor, but treat the emailed token as single-purpose: rotate/expire it on completion or decline, and document that email-link alone is a low-assurance factor so downstream users don't over-rely on it for high-value agreements.

capabilities.notes: No access-code concept exists. Recipient (domain/src/types.ts:43-59) has no accessCode/secretHash field; addRecipient (app.ts:190-198) and POST /api/envelopes/:id/recipients (http.ts:167-178) accept only name/email/role/routingOrder; resolveToken (app.ts:237-245) does no second-factor check before returning the session.
capabilities.recommendation: Add an optional per-recipient accessCode (store only a hash/HMAC), require it in getSession before revealing documents, rate-limit and lock after N failures, and record the challenge outcome in the audit log. This is the cheapest step-up factor and a common DocuSign default.

capabilities.notes: No phone number on Recipient, no OTP generation/verification, no SMS provider port anywhere (grep for otp/sms/phone across packages/server/src and packages/domain/src returns no auth code). The only delivery adapter is the email Mailer (server/src/mailer.ts).
capabilities.recommendation: Model a phone field + an OtpChallenge port (send/verify) with a pluggable SMS/voice provider, gate the signer session on a verified OTP, and audit each attempt. Requires a new domain concept of 'authentication requirement' per recipient (see step-up item).

capabilities.notes: No KBA anywhere in the codebase. Relevant for US notarial/regulated flows where DocuSign integrates a dynamic KBA (SSN/credit-header quiz) provider; FineSign has no identity-data provider port or challenge model.
capabilities.recommendation: Defer unless targeting regulated US e-notary/financial flows. If needed, integrate a third-party KBA provider behind a port (do not build in-house) and store only pass/fail + provider reference in the audit trail, never the underlying PII.

capabilities.notes: No document-upload-for-identity, selfie/liveness, or IDV provider integration. finesign-core/@finesign/pades handle document cryptography, not signer identity proofing; the Recipient model carries no verified-identity attributes.
capabilities.recommendation: Integrate a specialist IDV vendor (government-ID scan + liveness) behind a port for eIDAS 'qualified'/high-assurance or notary use cases; persist a verification reference and assurance level, not the raw ID images, and surface the assurance level on the certificate.

capabilities.notes: No IP is ever recorded. The audit events for viewing/signing carry only { recipientId } (domain/src/envelope-service.ts:278 markViewed, :315 recipient_signed) — no request context reaches the domain. grep for ip/x-forwarded/remoteAddress across server+domain finds nothing; Fastify's req.ip is available in http.ts but never read or threaded into applySignature/getSession. The certificate of completion lists recipient name/email/role/status + timestamps + document hashes only (server/src/certificate.ts).
capabilities.recommendation: Capture req.ip (with trustProxy/X-Forwarded-For configured) at getSession, applySignature, and decline; thread it into the audit event data and onto the certificate of completion. IP + timestamp in a tamper-evident log is the single most-cited evidentiary element of an e-signature audit trail — its absence materially weakens legal defensibility.

capabilities.notes: No user-agent or device fingerprint is recorded; same gap as IP — request headers are never propagated from http.ts into the audit data ({ recipientId } only).
capabilities.recommendation: Record the User-Agent string alongside IP and timestamp in each signer-action audit event and on the certificate, so the completion record shows what device/browser performed each action.

capabilities.notes: No geolocation (neither IP-derived nor browser Geolocation API). Not modeled on Recipient or in audit data.
capabilities.recommendation: Optionally derive coarse geo from the captured IP at render time (do not store precise coordinates by default, for privacy). Lower priority than IP/user-agent.

capabilities.capability: Consent to do business electronically (ESIGN/UETA e-consent disclosure)
capabilities.notes: No electronic-records consent step exists. There is no disclosure text, no consent checkbox/acceptance, and no consent audit event — AuditEventType (domain/src/types.ts:78-89) has no 'consent_given', and the signer session (getSession, app.ts:247-274) returns documents/fields with no gating disclosure. FieldKind includes checkbox but it is modeled-not-implemented (types.ts:25 comment) and is a document field, not a session-level consent gate.
capabilities.recommendation: Add a first-run e-consent gate: present the ESIGN/UETA disclosure, require explicit acceptance before the first signature, and write a hash-chained consent audit event (who/when/IP/disclosure-version) plus a line on the certificate. In the US this is a statutory prerequisite for an enforceable e-signature; its absence is a correctness gap, not just a feature gap.

capabilities.notes: The domain has no notion of an 'authentication requirement' per recipient or routing step — every recipient is authenticated identically by link possession. Recipient (types.ts:43-59) and addRecipient (app.ts:190-198) expose no auth-method field, so a sender cannot require, e.g., access code for signer A and OTP for signer B.
capabilities.recommendation: Introduce an authRequirements array on Recipient (e.g. ['email'] | ['email','accessCode'] | ['email','smsOtp']) enforced in resolveToken/getSession, and record which factors were satisfied in the audit trail. This is the structural prerequisite for the access-code/OTP/KBA items above.

capabilities.capability: Identity metadata on the certificate of completion
capabilities.notes: A certificate of completion IS generated (server/src/certificate.ts) and lists each recipient's name, email, role, status, timestamps, the hash-chained audit summary, and per-document SHA-256 hashes. But it records no authentication method, no IP/user-agent, and no consent acceptance for any signer — so it cannot evidence HOW each signer was identified, only that an email/name pair acted.
capabilities.recommendation: Once IP/user-agent/consent/auth-factor capture is added, render an 'Authentication' section per recipient on the certificate (factors satisfied, IP, device, consent version/time). This turns the certificate from a completion receipt into a legally-robust identity record.

parity.area: Compliance, Audit & Signature Assurance (DocuSign/Adobe Sign parity)

capabilities.capability: Certificate of Completion (human-readable trust summary appended to the sealed PDF)
capabilities.notes: server/src/certificate.ts buildCertificate() renders a standalone PDF with envelope title/id/status/timestamps, recipients (name, email, role, status, signedAt, declineReason), per-document SHA-256 hashes, and the hash-chained audit trail (seq/type/at/actor + truncated hash). appendCertificate() merges those pages onto the signed document (app.ts appendCertificate before sealing at line ~465-498), matching the DocuSign arrangement where the completed file carries its own certificate.
capabilities.recommendation: Solid baseline. Improve parity by adding per-recipient authentication method, IP address, and consent/disclosure acceptance to the certificate (see ESIGN capability), plus geolocation/user-agent. Consider a machine-readable (XML/JSON) sidecar and a QR/verification URL on the certificate page so a relying party can re-verify online.

capabilities.notes: domain/src/audit.ts implements an append-only, SHA-256 hash-chained log. hashEvent folds prevHash into each event and binds id/seq/type/at/actor/data via canonicalJson (recursively key-sorted, deterministic). verifyAuditChain checks contiguous seq (0..n-1), prevHash linkage, and hash recomputation, returning the first broken index. appendAuditEvent returns a new array (no mutation). This is genuinely tamper-EVIDENT.
capabilities.recommendation: Hash-chaining is tamper-evident, not tamper-PROOF: anyone who can rewrite the whole stored log can recompute a valid chain. Anchor the chain externally — periodically timestamp the tail hash via RFC 3161 (ties into B-T work) or publish/notarize it — so an attacker cannot silently rebuild history. Also ensure the DB layer enforces append-only (no UPDATE/DELETE grants) at the storage tier.

capabilities.capability: PAdES-B-B (basic cryptographic signature: detached CMS + mandatory signed attributes)
capabilities.notes: pades/src/cms.ts builds a detached RFC 5652 CMS SignedData with all four B-B signed attributes (content-type, signing-time, message-digest, signing-certificate-v2/ESS RFC 5035), correct DER SET-OF ordering, and re-tags [0]->0x31 before signing. sign.ts uses @signpdf with SUBFILTER_ETSI_CADES_DETACHED and whole-file incremental-update coverage. This is real, standards-conformant PAdES-B-B, Adobe/DSS-verifiable.
capabilities.recommendation: Production-ready for the platform-seal model. Verify Adobe Acrobat and EU DSS validator accept generated files in an interop test suite committed to CI. Add RSASSA-PSS support (the credential interface/ADR mention it but cms.ts only emits rsaEncryption PKCS#1 v1.5) for modern-crypto parity.

capabilities.capability: PAdES-B-T (RFC 3161 trusted timestamp proving signature existed at time T)
capabilities.notes: No implementation. oids.ts defines RFC 3161 timestamp OIDs and cms.ts BuildCmsParams accepts unsignedAttributes 'e.g. a signature timestamp for B-T', and types.ts SignatureVerdict carries a timestamp field — but nothing populates or verifies it. Task #25 'P4: PAdES-B-T timestamps' is still pending. verify.ts hardcodes timestamp:{present:false,valid:false,time:null} and never parses a TSA token. Signing time relies solely on the signer's own clock (signing-time signed attr), which is not trustworthy.
capabilities.recommendation: Highest-priority gap for legal credibility. Implement a TimestampAuthority port + RFC 3161 HTTP client, embed the timestamp token as an unsigned attr, and verify it in verifyPdf (populating the existing timestamp verdict). Without B-T, signatures can't be reliably dated and long-term validation is impossible. eIDAS qualified timestamps materially strengthen evidentiary weight.

capabilities.capability: PAdES-B-LT (long-term validation: embed cert chain + CRL/OCSP in the PDF DSS)
capabilities.notes: Only specified in ADR-0003 (levels table + phase P6) as a staged follow-on; no DSS/CRL/OCSP code exists. verify.ts validates the chain against a runtime trustStore but embeds no revocation material into the document. Once the seal certificate expires or revocation data ages out, third parties lose the ability to validate offline.
capabilities.recommendation: Implement DSS dictionary population (VRI/Certs/CRLs/OCSPs) after B-T lands. This is what makes an agreement verifiable years later — table stakes for contracts with long retention (real estate, employment, legal).

capabilities.capability: PAdES-B-LTA (long-term archive: document timestamp over the DSS, renewable)
capabilities.notes: Specified only (ADR phase P6). No archive/document-timestamp implementation. Needed to preserve integrity of validation material over decades and to allow timestamp renewal before algorithm obsolescence.
capabilities.recommendation: Sequence after B-LT. Provide an archive-timestamp refresh job. Positions FineSign for regulated/archival use cases (eIDAS long-term preservation).

capabilities.capability: Cryptographic vs. visual signatures (tamper-evidence embedded in the file itself)
capabilities.notes: FineSign layers both: visual overlay stamps for human signers plus one platform PAdES cryptographic seal over the final PDF (ADR decision 1; app.ts completeEnvelope stamps marks, appends certificate, then sealer.seal()). This is exactly the DocuSign/Adobe Sign model where humans are identified by audit+certificate and the platform provides the crypto seal.
capabilities.recommendation: Clearly document the trust model for customers: the crypto guarantee is a PLATFORM attestation of completed state, not per-signer PKI identity. For higher assurance/eIDAS AdES-per-signer, implement the per-signer certificate extension the ADR stages (per-user PKI enrollment, multiple signature fields, sequential incremental updates).

capabilities.capability: Independent signature verification (relying party can verify without the platform)
capabilities.notes: pades/src/verify.ts is a first-class verifier: recomputes ByteRange digest, verifies CMS, enforces WHOLE-DOCUMENT coverage (extractSignatures validates ByteRange geometry + trailing-bytes-are-whitespace, defeating the append/partial-coverage attack), checks message-digest + signing-certificate-v2 binding, validates chain (direct-trust pin or CertificateChainValidationEngine), enforces cert validity window, and rejects weak algos (SHA-1/MD5, MD5/SHA1-RSA, ECDSA-SHA1, RSA<2048). verifyDocument endpoint exposed in app.ts. Because the file is standard PAdES, Adobe Acrobat can also verify it independently.
capabilities.recommendation: Excellent and unusually rigorous. Add revocation checking (currently no OCSP/CRL at verify time) and surface the timestamp verdict once B-T exists. Publish a public verification web page/endpoint for counterparties, mirroring DocuSign's validation portal.

capabilities.capability: HSM/KMS-backed signing key protection (keys never exposed)
capabilities.notes: credential.ts/types.ts define a clean SigningCredential port: sign(tbs) returns only the signature, so CMS assembly never holds raw key material (HSM/KMS-ready seam, per ADR decision 3). But the ONLY implementation is LocalSigningCredential holding a software key in memory (from PKCS#12/PEM). No AWS KMS/CloudHSM/Azure Key Vault adapter ships. generateSelfSignedCredential exists for dev/test only.
capabilities.recommendation: Ship at least one real HSM/KMS credential adapter (AWS KMS asymmetric sign is a natural fit) before positioning as production e-signature infrastructure. DocuSign/Adobe use FIPS 140-2 HSMs for the sealing key; a software key on the app server is a materially weaker trust posture and a single point of compromise.

capabilities.capability: Trusted/qualified CA-issued signing certificate (vs. self-signed seal)
capabilities.notes: Architecture supports CA-issued certs (fromPkcs12 loads an org cert + chain; verify.ts supports chain-to-root trust). But the default posture is a directly-trusted platform seal (sealer.ts pins credential.certificate() as its own trust anchor), and the only generator produces a self-signed cert. A self-signed seal shows as 'not trusted by Adobe' unless the relying party manually trusts it.
capabilities.recommendation: For credibility, obtain a publicly-trusted / AATL (Adobe Approved Trust List) or eIDAS-qualified organizational certificate and document the production onboarding. Direct-trust pinning is fine for closed ecosystems but undercuts the 'anyone can verify in Acrobat' promise.

capabilities.capability: ESIGN / UETA consent, intent-to-sign, and disclosure capture
capabilities.notes: The audit trail (domain/src/audit.ts, generic AuditEventType events with actor/at/data) and certificate can record signing events, and recipient status/signedAt are captured. However there is no explicit evidence in the reviewed code of a structured Electronic Records and Signatures Disclosure consent step, an affirmative intent-to-sign act, or capture of authentication method/IP per signer as first-class audit fields required to robustly satisfy ESIGN/UETA.
capabilities.recommendation: Add explicit audit event types + certificate rows for: consent to do business electronically (with disclosure version accepted), intent-to-sign affirmation, authentication method, IP address, and timestamp per signer. These are the specific artifacts DocuSign surfaces to make an agreement defensible under ESIGN/UETA.

capabilities.capability: eIDAS positioning (AdES/QES levels, qualified trust services)
capabilities.notes: The engine is built to ETSI EN 319 142 PAdES profiles (ADR-0003) and is structurally capable of Advanced Electronic Signature quality. But without B-T/B-LT, per-signer qualified certs, or a Qualified Trust Service Provider timestamp, it cannot claim QES or even robust AdES-per-signer today; the platform seal is an organizational AdES-seal at best.
capabilities.recommendation: Decide and document target eIDAS tier. To credibly claim AdES, ship B-T + per-signer certs; QES requires a QTSP and QSCD (out of scope for self-host). Be precise in marketing to avoid overclaiming legal status.

capabilities.notes: No RFC 3161 TSA client or port implementation exists (see B-T). Only OID constants and interface hooks are present. All timestamps currently derive from server/signer clocks (signing-time attribute, audit 'at' strings), which are not independently trustworthy.
capabilities.recommendation: Same as B-T: integrate a configurable RFC 3161 TSA (e.g. a public/qualified TSA), use it for both signature timestamps and periodic audit-chain anchoring. This is the single most impactful assurance upgrade remaining.

capabilities.capability: Encryption at rest for stored documents and blobs
capabilities.notes: storage/src/blob-store.ts LocalFsBlobStore writes plaintext bytes via fs.writeFile with no encryption; InMemoryBlobStore stores raw bytes. Grep for encrypt/kms/aes/sse across storage/src returned nothing. Postgres/SQLite repositories store envelope data without any field/column encryption in the reviewed code. Recipient tokens ARE hashed before storage (tokenHash), which is good, but document content and PII are not encrypted at rest.
capabilities.recommendation: Add envelope/document encryption at rest: at minimum rely on documented KMS-backed volume/bucket encryption (S3 SSE-KMS for the S3 adapter), and ideally application-level envelope encryption for document blobs and PII columns. DocuSign/Adobe encrypt documents at rest with per-tenant keys — this is table stakes for handling signed agreements.

capabilities.capability: Data retention, deletion, and legal-hold policies
capabilities.notes: No retention/TTL/purge or legal-hold logic found (grep for retention/expire/ttl only surfaces recipient-token expiry in envelope-service.ts, not document retention). Blobs are written and never expired; there is no configurable retention window or verifiable deletion/erasure workflow.
capabilities.recommendation: Implement configurable retention policies, a deletion/erasure workflow (GDPR/CCPA right-to-erasure with audit of the deletion itself), and legal hold. Reconcile erasure with the immutability of the hash-chained audit and sealed PDFs (e.g. crypto-shredding keys rather than deleting audit events).

capabilities.capability: Fail-closed sealing (never deliver a 'completed' but unsealed document)
capabilities.notes: app.ts completeEnvelope enforces config.sealRequired: if sealing is required but no sealer is configured it throws ConflictError('SEAL_UNAVAILABLE') rather than delivering an unsealed completed document (ADR 'fail closed' invariant). Sealer only applies when configured, otherwise documents are explicitly delivered unsealed.
capabilities.recommendation: Good invariant. Make sealRequired the default in production config and add startup validation that the signing credential actually loads, so misconfiguration is caught at boot rather than at first completion.

capabilities.notes: packages/server/src/smtp-mailer.ts implements SmtpMailer over nodemailer behind an injectable MailTransport seam; makeNodemailerTransport() supports host/port/secure/auth. mailer.ts defines the Mailer port with ConsoleMailer (self-host default) and CapturingMailer (tests). app.ts notify() composes subject/text and delivers the signing link only via email, never logging it (S2).
capabilities.recommendation: Solid core. Add delivery-failure handling/retry (send is fire-and-forget after persist in persistThenDeliver) and a bounce/complaint feedback path so senders learn when a recipient never got the invite.

capabilities.notes: SmtpMailer.send() sends text-only bodies (transport.sendMail takes only {from,to,subject,text}); MailTransport interface has no html field. Notification copy is hard-coded English strings in app.ts notify() switch. No template engine, no logo, no sender-brand styling.
capabilities.recommendation: Add an html field to MailTransport/SentMessage and a minimal template layer (per-reason templates with sender name/logo). DocuSign/Adobe emails are branded; plain-text invites read as phishing and hurt open/complete rates.

capabilities.capability: Automatic reminders / nudges to pending signers
capabilities.notes: NotifyEffect.reason is only 'your_turn' | 'completed_copy' | 'declined' (packages/domain/src/effects.ts). Grep for remind/nudge/resend finds nothing except token-expiry logic (app.ts:241). Notifications fire only on state transitions (send, advance routing, decline). There is no scheduler, cron, or timer to re-notify a signer who hasn't acted.
capabilities.recommendation: Add a reminder scheduler (a NotifyEffect reason 'reminder' plus a background job that re-issues invites for recipients still 'notified' after N days, respecting tokenTtlMs). This is table-stakes for completion rates; envelopes stall without nudges.

capabilities.notes: http.ts exposes POST send/void/decline and field/recipient authoring, but no endpoint to resend an invite or reissue a token to an active recipient. The only token issuance path is app.send()/routing advance.
capabilities.recommendation: Add POST /api/envelopes/:id/recipients/:rid/resend that re-issues a fresh token (invalidating the prior hash) and fires a notify. Cheap to add and frequently requested.

capabilities.notes: No SMS/Twilio/phone code anywhere (grep sms|twilio empty). Recipients carry only name+email (http.ts addRecipient). Delivery is email-only; no phone-based OTP recipient authentication.
capabilities.recommendation: Introduce a Notifier/Channel abstraction alongside Mailer and an SMS adapter (e.g. Twilio) for delivery and SMS-OTP access control. Lower priority than reminders but expected by enterprise buyers for high-value agreements.

capabilities.notes: No webhook/callback/subscription code (grep empty). Lifecycle events (sent, viewed, signed, completed, declined, voided) exist internally as state transitions and audit entries but are never published outbound. Integrators can only poll GET /api/envelopes/:id.
capabilities.recommendation: Add webhook subscriptions with a signed (HMAC) payload delivered on each envelope/recipient state change, with retry + delivery log. This is the #1 integration primitive; DocuSign Connect / Adobe Sign webhooks are how every serious integration is built.

capabilities.notes: http.ts covers envelope CRUD-ish authoring (create, list, get, add document/recipient/field, send, void), public signer session (get/apply/decline/view doc), downloads (document, certificate) and verify. Missing: templates, bulk send, resend, recipient/field update/delete, envelope search/filtering (list is limit/offset only), webhook mgmt, user/account admin. Auth is a single shared senderApiKey (no per-account scoping/OAuth).
capabilities.recommendation: Fill gaps most integrators hit first: templates, bulk send, resend, and richer list filtering. Replace the single shared API key with per-account keys or OAuth for multi-tenant use.

capabilities.notes: http.ts registers @fastify/swagger + @fastify/swagger-ui; Swagger UI served at /docs and the raw document at /openapi.json, with a senderApiKey security scheme declared.
capabilities.recommendation: Strong. Add explicit request/response JSON schemas per route (bodies are currently cast from unknown with manual validation) so the generated spec documents payloads and enables typed client generation.

capabilities.capability: Embedded signing / iframe / signing ceremony SDK
capabilities.notes: A hosted signer page exists (packages/web/src/pages/Sign.jsx) driven by tokenized routes /sign/:token (http.ts), so signing links can be opened in a browser. But there is no embedded-signing SDK, no postMessage/iframe integration, no returnUrl/redirect, and no way to generate a recipient-view URL for embedding (grep iframe|embed|postMessage empty).
capabilities.recommendation: Add a 'create recipient view' endpoint returning a short-lived embeddable URL plus a small JS SDK that posts completion/decline events to the host via postMessage and supports a returnUrl. Embedded signing is a core DocuSign/Adobe feature for in-app flows.

capabilities.capability: Downloadable completed documents + certificate of completion
capabilities.notes: http.ts serves GET /api/envelopes/:id/documents/:documentId/download (signed PDF, attachment) and GET /api/envelopes/:id/certificate; certificate is appended into signed PDFs (task M6.1) and a PAdES verify endpoint exists (/documents/:documentId/verify). certificate.ts generates the completion certificate.
capabilities.recommendation: Add a single combined download (all documents + certificate as one PDF or a zip) for convenience, and expose the certificate/verify links in the completion email.

capabilities.capability: Branding / white-label (custom logo, colors, sending domain, custom URLs)
capabilities.notes: No branding/white-label config (grep brand|logo|whitelabel finds only the hard-coded '✒️ FineSign' brand link in web App.jsx:15). Emails carry a single global 'from' (SmtpMailer constructor) with no per-sender/per-account brand, and notification copy is fixed. baseUrl/signPath are global (app.ts), not per-tenant.
capabilities.recommendation: Add per-account branding (logo, colors, reply-to/from, custom email copy) applied in the email template and signer page. Buyers expect signing experiences to carry their own brand, not FineSign's.

capabilities.notes: No i18n/locale/translation code (grep empty). Email subjects/bodies are hard-coded English in app.ts notify(); the web signer UI has no locale switching. Recipients have no language preference field.
capabilities.recommendation: Externalize notification and signer-UI strings into a locale catalog keyed off a per-recipient language preference. Important for any non-English or cross-border deployment.
